You're basing this on the assumption that it's one or the other. Either we lose badly in the first round or we waste the season away and pray to the Hockey Gods we get lucky in what is now more than ever a complete crap shoot of who gets what. Both are terrible strategies for winning hockey games.  How many drafts did it take a struggling franchise to get their shit together?  A list of notable players drafted by that franchise.  Even after all that, it took literally the best player since a famous superstar to snap their franchise awake and finally get some blood pumping through those frozen arteries of theirs. And they *still* haven't done shit yet.  Planning your entire team strategy around winning the lottery and getting high draft picks, *especially* after they changed the lottery rules and *especially* with yet another team joining the league and making each draft pick less valuable, and expecting somehow to come out on top is frankly borderline retarded and isn't going to get you very far in today's league, especially when even at your most-injured and very worst you still can't lose as good as teams like a rival city or a struggling franchise.

Also in a pre-lockout, pre-salarycap and pre-lottery world.  This year was literally our worst season in 17 years. The very worst. And the *best* we got was fifth overall. That was with icing the worst lineup in recent memory, with a mind-blowingly high number of injuries to our most important and highest paid players, and even then we still walked away with no better than fifth overall.  Having a high draft pick helps. No one is arguing that.
